title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
I bring 20 years of senior leadership in Canadian hospitals, health authorities, and research institutes, including Chief Innovation Officer at the Health Sciences Centre in Winnipeg and senior roles at the Hotchkiss Brain Institute and Princess Margaret Hospital, together with a PhD in health economics and epidemiology & biostatistics from the University of Waterloo and an MBA from the Schulich School of Business.
Download my CV (PDF)

title: Research
text: My research examines whether health systems provide care to those who need it and how effectively they withstand periods of macroeconomic shocks and microeconomic stressors. I distinguish between potential access, the services people could, in principle, reach, and realized access, the services they actually use. I also model the factors that contribute to the gap between the two, including the impacts of climate change, infectious diseases, and health system capacity.

title: Research
text:
Current work
Health System Resilience in Western Province, Zambia (University of Waterloo, 2025–present). Using routine health information system data, I examine how seasonal flooding and other health system stressors affect the utilization of essential health care services, including maternal and child health services, infectious disease care, and general outpatient services.
The Economics of HIV Care in the HPTN 071 (PopART) Trial (Imperial College London, 2026–present). In collaboration with colleagues at Imperial College London, I model equity, economies of scale, and health care utilization costs in a cluster-randomized trial conducted in Zambia and South Africa.

title: Research
text:
Methods
My expertise includes frequentist and Bayesian modelling; econometrics, including interrupted time-series and difference-in-differences analyses; time-series forecasting; structural equation modelling; and geospatial analysis, including catchment-area and location-allocation methods. I primarily use R in my workflow.

title: Research
text:
Publications
Several manuscripts addressing climate shocks, malaria surveillance, maternal health care, and the economics of HIV care are currently under review or in preparation. A list of my publications is available on my Google Scholar profile.

title: Teaching
text: I teach health professionals to make better-informed decisions using evidence. Most of my students will become managers, analysts, clinicians, and executives rather than researchers. Accordingly, I focus on helping them ask the right questions of data, critically interpret the answers, and communicate their findings clearly to the people responsible for making decisions.

title: Teaching
text:
Value and Quality in Healthcare (MHIA 6160)
A graduate course I designed for the Master of Health Industry Administration program at the Schulich School of Business, York University, first offered in Winter 2027. Each module examines value and quality from both public-system and industry perspectives. Students develop data literacy through guided R laboratories, and the course concludes with a simulation capstone in which teams respond to a simulated epidemic and present their strategies to a mock national cabinet.

title: Cameron B. Chiarot, MBA, PhD
text:
I am a healthcare executive, educator, and health economist with 20 years of senior leadership experience in Canadian public-sector health organizations. I use quantitative modelling to examine health system resilience, access, and value, and educate health leaders to support informed, evidence-based decision-making.
Health systems frequently discuss access; however, they typically measure utilization. The gap between the two is where systems fail people, and it is where my work is focused.

Leadership
Senior leadership roles across hospitals, health authorities, and research institutes, encompassing capital programs valued at up to CAD $100 million, the development of new health facilities, and governance in the not-for-profit sector.


Research
Health system resilience to climate shocks in Western Province, Zambia, and the economics of the HPTN 071 (PopART) trial with Imperial College London. More on my research →


Teaching
Adjunct Professor at the Schulich School of Business, where I designed and teach Value and Quality in Healthcare (MHIA 6160), and Sessional Lecturer in the Master of Public Health program at the University of Waterloo. More on my teaching →

I am seeking leadership opportunities in applied research, innovation, and education across public agencies, health systems, research institutes, universities, and colleges. The best way to reach me is by email or LinkedIn.
